title: Google: Email sender guidelines
supports: Senders to Gmail need SPF or DKIM; senders of more than 5,000 messages a day to Gmail accounts need SPF, DKIM and DMARC, must support one-click unsubscribe for marketing and subscribed messages with List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers, and must keep the Postmaster Tools spam rate below 0.10% and avoid ever reaching 0.30%
limit: Page mentions Feb 1, 2024 and Dec 2023 start dates and no later revision date; thresholds and enforcement have changed before, so read the live page; it does not state an unsubscribe deadline, and a small sender below 5,000 a day is not held to the bulk rules but should still follow them

title: Yahoo Sender Hub: sender requirements and best practices
supports: Bulk senders implement SPF and DKIM and publish a DMARC policy of at least p=none that passes, keep spam rate below 0.3%, implement a list-unsubscribe header with one-click unsubscribe for marketing and subscribed messages (RFC 8058 POST highly recommended), and honour unsubscribes within 2 days
limit: Page says enforcement began in February 2024 and was rolled out gradually; it carries no revision date; the definition of a bulk sender and spam-rate basis sit elsewhere on Yahoo's site and were not read

title: FTC: CAN-SPAM Act compliance guide for business
supports: Commercial email needs accurate header information, a subject line that reflects the content, a clear disclosure that it is an advertisement, a valid physical postal address, a clear explanation of how to opt out, opt-outs honoured within 10 business days, and you cannot contract away responsibility for compliance; each violating email can bring penalties of up to $53,088
limit: United States law only and the penalty figure is inflation-adjusted, so confirm the current amount; it does not require prior consent, unlike the UK and EU rules

title: ICO: How do we comply with the PECR electronic mail marketing rules?
supports: UK rules for marketing email to individuals: consent must be freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous, with no pre-ticked boxes, silence or inactivity; consent is not transferable and must be easy to withdraw; the products and services soft opt-in has five listed conditions; every message must offer a simple, free opt-out
limit: UK law (PECR with UK GDPR), not EU member-state law or other regimes, though EU GDPR is similar in its consent definition; the page shows a 5 February 2026 date for the new charity rule and no other revision date; this is regulator guidance, not legal advice

title: Product Hunt Launch Guide: how Product Hunt works

title: Product Hunt Launch Guide: preparing for launch
supports: Tagline under 60 characters; description up to 500 characters; at least two gallery images; a first comment is not required, 70 percent of products reaching Product of the Day, Week or Month had one, and it should ask for feedback, not upvotes; the submission link must be the primary product page, and shortened or tracking links are not accepted

title: Product Hunt Launch Guide: sharing your launch

title: YouTube Help: how views are counted
supports: From August 24, 2026 a view is counted the moment a video starts to play, across Shorts, long-form videos and live streams; YouTube checks that views come from real people, which takes time, and counts can change after publication or be slowed, frozen or adjusted; Realtime shows only estimates

title: YouTube Help: check your impressions and watch time
supports: Thumbnail impressions are how many times thumbnails were shown to viewers on YouTube; an impression counts when the thumbnail is on screen for more than one second with at least half visible; impressions click-through rate is how often viewers watched a video after seeing the thumbnail
limit: A separate YouTube FAQ page, fetched, adds that impressions on external websites and end screens are not counted and views from other sources can make CTR differ from views divided by impressions; neither page gives a target CTR for a new channel

title: YouTube Help: determining if your content is made for kids

limit: Page is guidance, not legal advice, and no single factor decides; it does not itself list the feature restrictions, which sit on other YouTube Help pages not fetched here, so check them before relying on comments or other features for study-app audiences

title: YouTube Help: spam, deceptive practices and scams policy
supports: Titles, thumbnails and descriptions that trick users into clicking are prohibited; repetitive or deceptive comments and messages meant to drive traffic are spam; bots, coercion or rewards for likes, views or subscribers are prohibited while asking viewers to like, comment or subscribe is allowed; violations can bring removal, strikes or termination
limit: Fetched summary does not reproduce every example; enforcement judgments are YouTube's, and the page does not give thresholds

title: Search Console Help: what are impressions, position, and clicks
supports: Impressions are counted when a link to your site appears, including below the fold when no click on see more is needed; clicks are counted when a user goes from Google to a page outside Google; CTR is clicks divided by impressions; position uses the topmost position per query then averages across queries, and is recorded only when the link got an impression
limit: Page explains the metrics but not how well they predict real use; average position is an average over queries and not a live rank

title: Search Console Help: Performance report (Search results), about the data

title: App Review Guidelines
supports: Metadata including description, screenshots and previews must accurately reflect the app (2.3); keywords must not pack trademarked terms, popular app names or irrelevant phrases (2.3.7); 'For Kids' and 'For Children' in metadata are reserved for the Kids Category (2.3.8); apps outside the Kids Category cannot imply children are the main audience (5.1.4); Kids Category apps should not include third-party analytics or advertising and no links out or purchases outside a parental gate (1.3, 5.1.4); attempts to manipulate reviews or inflate rankings with paid, incentivized, filtered or fake feedback can lead to expulsion from the Developer Program (Section 3 introduction); apps must not force users to rate or review (3.2.2)

title: App Store Connect Analytics Help: Acquisition
supports: Unique Impressions are unique devices that viewed the app on the App Store; Unique Product Page Views are unique devices that viewed the product page; Total Downloads can be split into first-time downloads and redownloads and exclude iCloud restores and auto-downloads; Conversion Rate shows how often unique impressions turn into total downloads; source types are App referrer, Institutional Purchase, App Store browse, Web referrer, App Clip, App Store search and Unavailable; data is attributed to the source recorded at the most recent download and manual redownloads reset it
limit: Does not separately define 'first-time download'; promo-code and gift-card downloads show source Unavailable; the filters reference states App Store dimensions need at least five first-time downloads; the separate Metric definitions page was not read

title: App Store Connect Analytics Help: Campaign links
supports: Campaign links are URLs with provider (pt), campaign (ct) and media type (mt) tokens, created under Apps > Analytics > Acquisition > Campaigns; they capture impressions, product page views, downloads, usage, sales and subscriptions per campaign token; a first-time download counts if within 24 hours of using the link; only the most recent link is credited; campaigns display after 24 hours and need at least five first-time downloads from individual users
limit: Campaigns tab needs the app to have analytics data first; small groups can be withheld or combined in the detailed API reports; credit window and last-link rule mean tagged counts are not every download from a channel

title: Apple Developer Help: Enroll in the Apple Developer Program
supports: The Apple Developer Program annual fee is 99 USD (prices may vary by region); accredited educational institutions can enroll with a fee waiver; organizations can buy a membership only after Apple verifies the enrollment information; if no confirmation arrives within 24 hours of purchase, contact Apple
limit: No processing time for organization verification is stated; no fee waiver for individuals; App Review timing is on a separate Apple page (stated there as at least 50% of submissions in under 24 hours and 90% in under 48 hours) which is not cited here

title: Play Console Help: User Ratings, Reviews, and Installs
supports: Any manipulation of ratings, reviews or install counts is prohibited; do not offer rewards or incentives for ratings or reviews (sample violation: a discount in exchange for a high rating); do not repeatedly submit ratings posing as users; prompt for a rating in a clear, non-deceptive way and do not force users to rate; replies to reviews should not ask for a higher rating
limit: Page carries no revision date; the separate metadata policy (no ranking claims like '#1', no unattributed testimonials, 30-character titles) was read at /answer/9898842 but is not cited as a ref; the fetched text did not detail incentivized-install rules beyond the summary

title: Play Console Help: Google Play Families Policies
supports: If a target audience for the app is children, the Families requirements apply; the target audience age group must be declared before publishing; store listings promoting play for children must match the app; ads to children or users of unknown age must use Families Self-Certified Ads SDKs without interest-based advertising; apps solely targeting children must not transmit the advertising ID; mixed-audience apps need a neutral age screen; the privacy policy must reflect data practices
limit: Page does not mention teens or analytics SDKs by name and gives no age cut-offs in the text read, so whether a teen-focused app is covered depends on the audience you declare; page is a policy summary, not the full SDK program rules

title: Play Console Help: Measure your app's acquisition and retention
supports: Store listing visitors are unique users who visited the store listing on the Play Store app but have not installed the app; first-time installers are unique users who installed some days after visiting the listing; installs without store listing visit are unique users who installed without seeing the listing or had it pre-installed; charts show conversion from one segment to the next; Tracked channels (UTM) are unique users who visited the listing from a UTM-tagged link and untagged links fall under third-party referrers; data below minimum thresholds is not displayed or is grouped as Other
limit: Page does not define store listing acquisitions or conversion formally; the Statistics page (answer 139628) defines install events, user acquisitions and device acquisition differently and reports installs in Pacific Time; search extracts mention a July 2026 shift to click-based listing metrics that the fetched pages did not confirm

title: Play Console Help: Get started with Play Console
supports: There is a US$25 one-time registration fee payable by listed credit or debit cards (prepaid not accepted); a government ID and credit card in the legal name may be requested and the fee is not refunded if the information is invalid; personal accounts created after November 13, 2023 must meet testing requirements before release and verify access to an Android device
limit: Page does not state app review time (the publishing page, answer 9859751, says standard updates are processed as soon as possible and some reviews can take up to 7 days or longer in exceptional cases, but it is not cited here); testing requirement details are on a separate page

title: Poki for Developers: how we partner with you (revenue and deal types)
supports: Poki offers two agreement types. Web exclusive is its preferred way: on the open web the game is published only on Poki, which covers browser, Discord and YouTube Playables, and by default runs for 5 years; Steam, mobile app stores and consoles are not part of the exclusivity. Non-exclusive is a one-time flat licence fee with no revenue share, for games already live on other web platforms or with a niche or short-term fit
limit: Poki calls the 5-year term, the revenue share and the investment indicative and says the real terms are set out in the agreement; the page does not say whether an own-site build may stay live under an exclusive deal; the 100% and 50/50 revenue split is on the working-with-Poki page, not here

title: Poki for Developers: working with Poki
supports: Every game on Poki is hand-picked; revenue from a player who arrives directly (bookmarks, search, social media or your own community) is 100% yours, and revenue from a player who arrives through Poki.com or a Poki marketing effort is split 50/50; Poki asks for web exclusivity in return for its investment while Steam, app stores and consoles stay yours
limit: Describes the exclusive deal in general terms and does not mention the non-exclusive option that the deal-types page offers; the figures are Poki's own and indicative

title: Poki for Developers: requirements and quality standards
supports: Hard requirements: desktop, mobile and tablet support, 16:9 scaling, localStorage wrapped for incognito mode, no external requests, no branding or external ads, playable with an ad blocker. Correct SDK events (gameplayStart on the first input, gameplayStop on any interruption, commercialBreak only when leaving a pause) are required for web fit testing and every release. In-app purchases and other ad systems are not allowed, and external links go through PokiSDK.openExternalLink
limit: Lists what Poki QA checks, not what Poki accepts; says nothing about how a build made for itch.io or Steam must change beyond these rules

title: Poki for Developers: how testing works
supports: Five steps: add the game, playtests (10 recordings each), a player fit test (500 players, playtime only), a web fit test (about 7 days on real category pages, measuring click-through rate, time on page and conversion to play against category averages) and a final review in 1 to 2 weeks. A healthy player fit result is 3+ minutes average playtime with 25%+ of plays over 3 minutes; Poki suggests aiming for 65%+ conversion to play and 5+ minutes average playtime before requesting review. Tests are free and repeatable
limit: The thresholds are Poki's own floors for moving forward and the 70% and 6+ minute averages are its own claim, not a forecast for another game; the pages read name conversion to play without defining its numerator and denominator

title: Poki for Developers: release process
supports: After an agreement the game goes through QA against the requirements, a soft release of about 2 to 3 weeks that cannot be skipped (the developer must be available to ship fixes) and then global release. During soft release Poki expects the developer to monitor conversion to play and engagement, errors, monetization (at least 1 ad per daily active user) and player feedback
limit: Timings are Poki's estimates; the page does not say how a rejected QA report affects the schedule

title: Poki for Developers: final review
supports: The final review takes 1 to 2 weeks and judges the test results, the game's quality and originality and whether it is unique enough within its categories; after a pass the legal, QA, soft release and global release steps take roughly 2 to 3 months in total; a failed review means Poki sees no fit at that time
limit: The 1 to 2 week and 2 to 3 month figures are Poki's estimates; a game that does not pass cannot be published on Poki at that time, and Poki invites other submissions

title: Poki for Developers: external resources policy
supports: Poki blocks all external requests by default: no external assets, in-game chat or external account systems. Analytics, leaderboards and multiplayer servers can be approved case by case through Settings, CSP in Poki for Developers with a hosted privacy policy; Google products, including Google Analytics, cannot be approved
limit: Says nothing about which analytics providers are approved in practice; a build that reports tagged visits or returns to its own analytics needs an approved exception first

title: Poki for Developers: content and player safety, quality guidelines and AI
supports: Games must suit all ages and chat is not allowed. Poki favours original, polished, web-first games and declines clones. On AI it says the game should reflect the developer's own perspective and meaningful improvement beyond the base tooling before the fit tests, and that developers should be able to show which tools were used, and their prompts and iterations, on request because AI-only creation can raise ownership issues
limit: Poki reserves the right to decline any game that lacks originality even when it works and cannot always explain a decline; the page gives no view on the ownership of AI-assisted art

title: CrazyGames Documentation: technical requirements
supports: Total file size up to 250 MB and 1,500 files; initial download up to 50 MB (20 MB for the mobile homepage). With the SDK the initial download is measured from the start of loading to the first Gameplay start event; without the SDK total file size is used and must be 50 MB or less (20 MB for the mobile homepage). Relative paths only; the game should work in Chrome and Edge and smoothly on a 4 GB Chromebook
limit: Does not address service workers, offline packs or caching; externally hosted files are judged on time to reach gameplay (20 seconds or less); limits are CrazyGames' own and can change

title: CrazyGames Documentation: requirements overview
supports: Two launch steps: Basic Launch (the SDK is optional and monetization is not available) and Full Launch (all requirements including the SDK, with ads served only through it). Basic requirements include PEGI 12 and no external ads. The Developer Dashboard shows players, average playtime, gameplay conversion, retention and revenue
limit: A summary table; the revenue-share percentage and payment terms are not stated on it, and the developer terms page returned a not-found page when fetched

title: CrazyGames Documentation: Basic Launch guide, the metrics that matter
supports: Basic Launch ends once the game has been live at least 7 days and has reached at least 500 plays, or after 21 days. The dashboard updates daily and tracks average play time (the average time a player spends in a single session), Day 1 retention (the percentage of players who come back the day after their first session) and conversion (the percentage of players who play at least one minute after starting). No SDK is needed and ads stay disabled
limit: The 10+ minute, 10 to 15 percent and 80+ percent benchmarks describe successful or strong titles per CrazyGames and are not thresholds for Full Launch; the percentages' denominators are not defined further

title: CrazyGames Documentation: gameplay requirements
supports: English localization is required and content must be original. No cross-promotion, with exceptions: community links that do not lead directly to a playable web version, store links for desktop games only on the main menu or at the end of a demo, and links to games in the same series; app store links are never allowed in the game. The audience is aged 13 or more and the game must be PEGI 12 compliant
limit: The link exceptions apply only when the link is not a main call to action on the menu; the page does not say how strictly each is enforced

title: CrazyGames Documentation: FAQ and contact
supports: A game already live elsewhere can be published if you hold the distribution rights, and the developer keeps 100% ownership. CrazyGames hosts the uploaded files on its CDN, does not iframe games hosted on competing browser game portals, and treats a build on your own domain as a regular submission that earns revenue only with a correctly integrated SDK. Rankings rest on play count, average playtime, retention, conversion and player feedback; players who leave a negative rating are asked why. Payments are monthly once the balance reaches EUR 100
limit: The accordion answers needed the full page text rather than the visible text; the revenue-share percentage is not stated; the developer terms were not read

title: CrazyGames Documentation: payouts
supports: Monthly payouts run through Tipalti after onboarding in the Developer Portal, by wire transfer, direct deposit or ACH, eCheck or PayPal depending on country, with a minimum of EUR 100 in earnings before a payout
limit: Fees and thresholds vary by method and country; CrazyGames gives no legal, tax or financial advice

title: Newgrounds Wiki: Game Guidelines
supports: You must be the creator and owner of the game and have rights to its music. On AI: do not share any games that were generated via an AI prompt (shovelware), disclose what and how AI was used in the author commentary, and do not use an AI-generated thumbnail; AI voice is allowed in some cases. Enforcement is subjective and AI-assisted work may be removed at Newgrounds' discretion. The game must work in a web browser without a download, must not auto-redirect or open pop-ups, and should not rely on third-party servers (tracking needs notice and an opt-out)
limit: The page calls AI an evolving area and does not say whether agent-authored procedural art or synthesized sound counts as generated via an AI prompt; a game removed after judging should not be resubmitted without noticeable improvements

title: Newgrounds Wiki: Game Dev Resources
supports: A majority of games are now HTML5; an HTML5 export is uploaded as a .zip whose root contains index.html, which is the file Newgrounds loads
limit: No size or file-count limit appears on this page, and a separate HTML5 guide URL returned a not-found page when fetched

title: Newgrounds Wiki: Monetization
supports: Newgrounds is attempting to transition to being ad free for everyone, with a revenue-sharing system as a goal once there are enough paying supporters; the revenue program and Flash ad information on the page are described as legacy systems that are no longer active
limit: Does not say whether a replacement revenue-sharing system exists today

title: Newgrounds Wiki: Frequently Asked Questions (Game Portal)
supports: Users judge new submissions by voting 0 to 5, and a submission can be blammed (removed) or protected; users can post and delete reviews; games can carry medals
limit: The page does not define the Views, vote or review counts shown on a game page, so copy the label you read into the observation definition

title: Game Jolt Help Docs: add your game
supports: A game page needs a description, tags and a maturity rating (All Ages, Teen or Mature). Thumbnails must be 16:9, at least 588x331 pixels and at most 30 MB; headers 900 to 5120 pixels wide with a ratio from 2.7 to 6.3. Builds are organised in packages and versioned releases (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) that start hidden until published; a browser build is added by platform such as HTML. Game Jolt provides metrics for each release. Comments and ratings can be switched off per game, ratings are likes and dislikes that feed the game's voltage, and people follow game pages
limit: The page names no size limit for HTML builds and does not list the analytics metrics, so their names were not captured

title: Game Jolt Help Docs: requirements for becoming a Creator
supports: Game Jolt users with 1,000 followers and quality content, or creators with 3,000 followers on another platform such as TikTok, Instagram, Twitch or YouTube, are considered for Creator status
limit: Creator status is a Game Jolt choice, not a right; the page is short and gives no review time

title: Game Jolt Help Docs: getting paid
supports: Creators earn from charged stickers (a share of the day's Game Jolt ad revenue, converted to Gems worth 1 cent USD each, held 7 business days) and from shop sales; the minimum withdrawal is $20 (2,000 Gems), paid by PayPal, wire transfer or ACH
limit: Sticker value changes daily with platform ad revenue and Creator status is needed to earn from them

title: Game Jolt Help Docs: site guidelines
supports: Spam includes off-topic posts, excessive tagging, duplicate posts, repeated posting in quick succession, links to off-topic or monetized external websites and bots or scripts that post, like and follow at inhumane rates; uploading a game you did not create counts as theft; each Community adds its own rules
limit: No rule on AI-generated content appears in the guidelines read, which is not permission; the livestreaming section is outdated

title: Gamedev Mastodon (mastodon.gamedev.place): about
supports: An independent server for game development and related topics run by one administrator, with about 4.2K active users, a code of conduct and usage guidelines; the page says feeds are chronological with no algorithms or ads
limit: Describes one server; other Mastodon servers have other topics, rules and sizes; the active-user figure is the server's own count

title: Gamedev Mastodon: instance data (API v2)
supports: New accounts need approval and a reason; posts are limited to 500 characters and 4 media attachments, with each link counted as 23 characters; six server rules cover sensitive media, hate, violence, harassment, content illegal in the EU and intentionally false or misleading information
limit: Machine-readable settings read on one day; the six rules do not mention promotion, which is not permission because the code of conduct and usage guidelines also apply

title: Gamedev Mastodon: usage guidelines
supports: The server is for game developers and people interested in game development, across all specialities and experience levels; the local timeline is mostly about game development, the preferred language is English, and the administrator notes a smaller network means fewer people to interact with
limit: The page does not address promotion of your own game or links to playable builds

title: Mastodon documentation: posting to your profile
supports: The default limit is 500 characters; links must start with http(s):// and count as 23 characters, and link shorteners are discouraged; a post can carry up to 4 images or one video or audio file; only Public posts appear in public feeds and search; hashtags make a post discoverable and media descriptions are recommended
limit: Software defaults that each server can change; the page describes no analytics, so reach is not measurable from it

title: Steamworks Documentation: Curators and Curator Connect
supports: Curator Connect needs at least a public coming-soon page and the Generate CD Keys permission; a developer can send offers to 100 curators with a maximum of 5 copies each, and curators have no obligation to accept, play or review
limit: Steam only, so a browser-only game with no Steam page has nothing to offer here; the page gives no acceptance or coverage rate

title: Steamworks Documentation: Steam keys
supports: Developers launching their first game wait three weeks after the AppID is created before requesting keys; Release State Override keys are generally limited to 2,500 total; free products cannot request keys by default and must submit a ticket; giveaways are disallowed unless very small (under 100 keys); Valve warns of fraudsters impersonating journalists or storefronts to obtain keys for resale
limit: Rules and limits are Valve's and can change; key handling does not apply to a free browser game

title: Steamworks Documentation: Steam Next Fest, February 2027
supports: The February 2027 edition runs February 22 to March 1 (10:00 AM PST); registration closes January 10, 11:59pm PST, and all required items are due February 8. Eligibility: a published public store page, a publicly playable demo by the start, not a prologue or demo of existing content, a release after March 1, 2027, and a game may appear in only one Next Fest
limit: Each edition has its own page (October 2026 closed to registration on August 31; June 2027 registration closes April 25); dates were read on 2026-10-11 and Valve can change them; a public store page needs the paid Steam Direct fee first

title: Wholesome Games
supports: The organizer's FAQ states 'We stand firmly against AI-generated art and NFTs'; the site points to a mailing list for a reminder when the next submission form is live
limit: A stance, not a form rule: a separate Wholesome Games Presents publishing form asks whether generative AI was used (not at all, for planning or prototyping such as concept art, or included in the game or marketing materials), and the Wholesome Direct showcase form was not live; whether agent-authored procedural art counts is not answered

title: Comfy Cozy Gaming: cozy games coming in August 2026
supports: The post states 'We do our best not to highlight cozy games that use Generative AI at any level of development or marketing' and that the listed games have not reported or disclosed using it
limit: An editorial statement in one monthly roundup post dated 2026-07-31, not a standalone policy page; no other outlet's AI policy was found

title: presskit.gg: the complete guide to indie game press kits
supports: Vendor and practitioner guidance: one public press page with a factsheet, short and long descriptions, 6 to 12 screenshots at 1920x1080 or larger without watermarks, a trailer, logos, team information and a contact email, kept current at each milestone
limit: Written by the vendor of a press kit plugin and quoting journalists' preferences; no source read measures whether a press kit changes coverage

title: Keymailer pricing (developer side now Partnier)
supports: The page says it is always free for content creators and that the developer login has been rebranded to Partnier; it publishes no developer price and asks visitors to book a demo
limit: Vendor marketing; reach figures such as 60,000+ influencers are the vendor's own claims; a third-party review's $24.99 a month entry tier was not verified

title: Lurkit pricing
supports: Paid creator campaigns ('Quests') carry a 20% commission fee per Quest, plan prices are 'Contact for pricing', and the page invites applications for up to a 70% discount
limit: Vendor marketing; no developer price list is published, so cost cannot be planned from it

title: Kotaku: Opening Night Live games with generative AI (2026-08-26)
supports: Press checks games against Steam's AI disclosure: Kotaku listed Gamescom Opening Night Live games using generative AI and wrote that it had seen several examples of developers not disclosing genAI use on Steam until they had been caught
limit: One outlet's article about one event; secondary reporting, not a platform rule

title: Poki for Developers: what we look for
supports: Poki curates on quality (UX, feel and the core game loop), player fit and tech (fast load times, stable frame rates and a lean file size on mobile and desktop web); beyond that it looks for originality, depth and replayability, a clear first impression, cross-device feel and room to grow. It says its audience is majority mobile, so a desktop-only game is at a disadvantage, and that the criteria are weighed together rather than scored against a pass mark
limit: Poki's own criteria for its own curation; it publishes no acceptance rate

title: Game Jolt Help Docs: growth and analytics
supports: The Creator HUD has an analytics dashboard showing where viewers come from and which content resonates; the guide recommends diversifying content, consistent posting, polls and sharing your Game Jolt link on other channels
limit: Written for Creators and aimed at shop and sticker revenue; it names no analytics metrics and gives no reach or conversion figures

title: Steam Page Analyzer: how to get streamers to play your game (2026 outreach playbook)
supports: Vendor view: cold outreach to creators who have never heard of you typically gets single-digit response rates and zero is a normal early result, while opt-in platforms do better; creators check in the first seconds whether they can play now, whether it looks like content and whether it fits their channel; one developer who emailed about 30 creators got no replies
limit: A vendor blog selling related tools, so its coverage figures are marketing claims; no measured reply rate exists and the 30-email case is one anecdote

title: Steamworks Documentation: Store Graphical Assets
supports: Required store capsule sizes: header 920x430, small 462x174, main 1232x706, vertical 748x896; optional page background 1438x810. Header, main and vertical capsules must not carry quotes or other text beyond the game's title. Screenshots must show only gameplay (no concept art, pre-rendered cinematic stills, awards or marketing copy): at least 5, 1920x1080 minimum at 16:9, with at least four marked suitable for all ages so the game can appear in some front-page places
limit: Undated page. A callout dated August 2024 in one capture said larger capsule sizes are accepted and old dimensions no longer are; two later renders did not show it, so recheck sizes in Steamworks. Stricter about capsule text than the rules page (see steam-assets-rules); the four all-ages screenshots are worded 'should'

title: Steamworks Documentation: Library Assets
supports: Library capsule 600x900, library header 920x430, library hero 3840x1240 with an 860x380 safe area and no text, and a library logo as a transparent PNG 1280 px wide and/or 720 px tall holding only the logotype. Library assets are visible only for apps with a published store page
limit: Undated page. It asks for no text beyond the title on the library capsule, while the rules page allows the logo plus an official subtitle there; see steam-assets-rules

title: Steamworks Documentation: Graphical Asset Rules
supports: Content on base store capsules is limited to game artwork, the game name and any official subtitle: no review scores, award names or logos, discount copy, calls to action such as 'Wishlisting now available', promotion of another product, or other text. Update text is allowed only in a temporary Artwork Override localized to the game's languages. Library capsule: logo (and subtitle if appropriate); library hero: no words; library logo: logotype only on a transparent background. Capsules need a readable logo or name, accurate dimensions and PG-13 art; games that break the rules can lose store visibility and eligibility for official sales and events
limit: Page says the rules took effect 2022-09-01. Neither this page nor steam-assets-standard says whether a tagline counts as an 'official subtitle', and the standard page asks for the title only, so plan title-only capsules

title: Steamworks Documentation: Trailers
supports: Upload up to 1920x1080 at 30 or 60 fps and 5,000+ Kbps as .mov, .wmv or .mp4 (H.264 and AAC preferred, 16:9 preferred). The first two valid trailers show before any screenshots. Valve highly recommends a first trailer that is primarily gameplay, and notes that a customer may give a game less than 10 seconds or watch without audio. Steam builds a 6-second microtrailer from six 1-second clips of the first video, which cannot be customized. A custom poster must be a 1920x1080 frame from the video, and a game cannot be released while a trailer is converting
limit: The gameplay-first and HUD-visible lines are recommendations, not requirements, and the page gives no length guidance

title: Steamworks Documentation: Review Process
supports: Store presence review typically takes 3-5 business days and should be requested at least 7 business days before going live; the page may only contain features and content available at launch, capsules need a readable title or logo and screenshots only gameplay. Build review also takes 3-5 business days (plan 7): the product must start properly on every operating system listed on the store page, listed features must exist, and in-game transactions must use Steam Wallet, so a build may not link to stores that do not offer it
limit: Other Valve pages give 1-5 days for the same reviews (see steam-onboarding). No Steamworks page read mentions Electron, NW.js or HTML5 wrappers, so wrapper acceptance is neither banned nor confirmed until a build passes review

title: Steamworks Documentation: Onboarding
supports: A 21-day waiting period between paying the app fee and releasing; a public coming-soon page for at least two weeks; page and build review of 1-5 days; tax information verified by a third party in 10 to 15 business days; a $100 fee per product
limit: Contradicts the Steam Direct page (steam-direct), which states a 30-day waiting period, and the Getting Started FAQ (steam-gs-faq), which gives 2-7 business days for tax verification. Plan on the longer figures and ask Valve before paying

title: Steamworks Documentation: Getting Started FAQ
supports: Tax information is verified by a third party in 2-7 business days, and a recently issued taxpayer number can take up to 30 days because of IRS validation
limit: The onboarding page says 10 to 15 business days for the same step. The Distribution Agreement, which would state the minimum age of a seller, is behind a Steamworks login and was not read

title: Steamworks Documentation: Content Survey
supports: The survey must be completed before the store page and build go to review. Its generative AI part covers content that ships with the game and is consumed by players (artwork, sound, narrative, localization); efficiency gains from AI-powered development tools are not its focus. Pre-Generated is content made with AI tools during development; Live-Generated is content made while the game runs and also needs a description of guardrails. Valve evaluates AI output like any other content and holds the developer to the Distribution Agreement promise that the game is non-infringing and consistent with its marketing materials. The general part generates regional ratings shown on the store page
limit: The actual questions are behind a Steamworks login and were not read. A news report says Valve rewrote this section in January 2026, and the page read already carries that wording. The page does not say how agent-written code or text is treated

title: Steam Subscriber Agreement
supports: You may not become a Steam Subscriber if you are under the age of 13; Steam is not intended for children under 13 and Valve will not knowingly collect personal information from them; additional age restrictions may apply in your country
limit: Binds account holders, not developers or players who never sign in; the age needed to sell on Steam is in the Distribution Agreement, which is behind a Steamworks login and was not read

title: itch.io Creator Documentation: Uploading HTML5 games
supports: A ZIP containing index.html with at most 1,000 files after extraction, paths up to 240 characters, 500 MB extracted and 200 MB for any single file; relative paths are required and absolute paths starting with / fail. HTML5 games take payments only as donations; selling access needs Kind of Game set to Downloadable
limit: Undated page; the limits are worded 'should not' and itch.io invites contact if they do not fit. Whether an offline service worker registers inside itch.io's embedding frame was not tested

title: itch.io Creator Documentation: Quality guidelines
supports: Asks creators to accurately tag generative AI use through the AI Disclosure section of the project edit page; projects that disclose appear on the AI Assisted browse page; self-contained algorithms such as procedural level generation and dynamic music need no tag. Under spam, it says not to use automated systems to mass produce product pages, and lists games predominantly created by algorithms or AI with minimal human intervention among content that may be removed from browse and search; AI use should be clearly stated in the project description
limit: For game pages the wording is 'we ask that you tag'; strict enforcement and delisting are stated for asset pages. The spam clause concerns excessive or mass-produced content, so how it applies to one agent-made game is a judgment itch.io has not published

title: itch.io staff post: Generative AI Disclosure tagging
supports: The project edit page asks whether a project contains generative AI and, if so, which kinds: Graphics, Sound, Text & Dialog and Code. A yes adds the AI Generated tag and sub-tags and a no adds No AI. The field is required for asset creators, whose untagged generative AI assets are no longer indexed on browse pages; staff replies encourage everyone else to fill it in and say code synthesized by a large language model counts
limit: A staff post and replies in a community forum, not a policy page, so the rule can change without notice. It makes disclosure mandatory only for asset pages. It reads LLM-written code as generative AI content, which is stricter than Steam's survey (steam-content-survey)

title: GitHub Docs: GitHub Pages limits
supports: A Pages site may be no larger than 1 GB and has a soft bandwidth limit of 100 GB per month; GitHub may not be able to serve a site that exceeds its quotas. Pages is not intended to run an online business, an e-commerce site or another site primarily for commercial transactions or SaaS
limit: Undated page. It says nothing about visit analytics for a Pages site, so 'Pages has no analytics of its own' is an inference from silence; the repository Traffic graph (github-traffic-guide) describes the repository, not the Pages site

title: Federal Register: Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule, final rule (2025-04-22)
supports: The amended COPPA Rule took effect June 23, 2025; except for a few provisions, regulated entities had until April 22, 2026 to comply
limit: A rule text, not legal advice. COPPA's duties attach to services directed to children under 13 or with actual knowledge of them that collect personal information; whether a given game is child-directed, and what the UK Children's Code or GDPR Article 8 add, were not researched

title: eCFR: 16 CFR 312.2, COPPA definitions
supports: Personal information includes a persistent identifier that can be used to recognize a user over time and across websites or services, such as a customer number held in a cookie, an IP address or a device identifier. Whether a service is directed to children weighs subject matter, visuals, animated characters, music and the evidence of intended audience, including marketing or promotional materials or plans; a mixed-audience service is not deemed directed to children for a visitor not identified as under 13
limit: The browser page blocks automated readers, so the text was read through the eCFR API (issue date 2026-10-07). Definitions only, not legal advice; it does not say whether the IP address a static host logs counts when the game itself collects nothing

title: GameDiscoverCo: What do Steam fans really think about AI disclosures
supports: About 3,800 Steam players (a ~16,000 panel, fielded June 25 to July 2, 2026): 43% have no major issue buying a game with an AI disclosure, 26% are neutral and 31% negative; 44% read disclosures in detail and 45% glance; 17% believe developers fully disclose; 56% say AI coding helpers should be disclosed and 8% disagree
limit: The publisher calls its panel more committed than the average Steam player. The 8% who would refuse to buy is reported as a share of all respondents by one write-up (PC Guide, captured) and of the negative group by another, so the denominator is unsettled. Read through a summarizing fetch tool and a verbatim capture of the PC Guide report, not the newsletter's charts

title: GamesMarket on Quantic Foundry: Most gamers are negative about Gen AI in video games (2025-12-22)
supports: Quantic Foundry's optional survey (N = 1,799, October to December 2025): 85% negative toward Gen AI in games and 63% at the most negative option; AI-generated quests and dialogue were 77% and 83% negative against 46% for a combined item in 2024; Story and Design motivations correlate negatively with approval (r = -0.12 each)
limit: Read through this secondary write-up because Quantic's own page is behind a Cloudflare challenge. The sample is 74% core and 21% hardcore gamers and 5% casual, 90% PC and aged 13 and over, so it under-represents casual and cozy players. The 2024 and 2025 figures come from different surveys

title: Windows Central on Game Oracle: AI disclosure and Steam reviews
supports: Game Oracle studied almost 10,000 Steam releases from January to October 2025: games disclosing AI averaged 4 reviews in the first month against 7, and 84.6% against 88.3% positive at 100+ reviews; its causal model put disclosing games at about 53% fewer reviews, with a larger drop for established studios and little for inexperienced ones with no marketing budget
limit: A vendor's model reported by a news site; reviews stand in for sales and the cause of the gap is not established. Not peer reviewed and the model was not inspected

title: arXiv 2608.11539: Player Perceptions of Generative AI in Games: A Steam Review Analysis
supports: Across 508,192 English-language Steam reviews, games disclosing generative AI received lower recommendation rates and more negative sentiment than games using procedural content generation; thematic analysis of 600 reviews found players read generative AI as low developer investment
limit: A preprint, not peer reviewed, and only the abstract was read. English reviews of games that disclosed; it does not isolate disclosure from the game's quality or from who chooses to disclose

title: Steam store search with tag filters
supports: Tag-filtered store search returns a total count for any tag combination, for example Farming Sim plus Space, which is how a niche's supply is counted
limit: Undocumented and community-tagged, so counts are lower bounds that drift daily. The total depends on the sort: Farming Sim plus Space returned 18 sorted by Reviews_DESC (which silently drops games under 10 reviews), 30 by Released_DESC (released games only) and 60 by relevance (which includes unreleased pages). Record the query, sort and date with any count

title: USPTO Trademark Search
supports: The official search of US federal trademark applications and registrations, including class, status and owner
limit: An interactive page: automated readers returned 'No results found' even for a known registered mark, so search it in a browser or read a registration page directly. It covers US federal marks only, not state, foreign or unregistered use. Marketing prior-art research, not legal clearance

title: WebKit: Full Third-Party Cookie Blocking and More (Intelligent Tracking Prevention)
supports: Safari deletes all of a website's script-writable storage after seven days of Safari use without user interaction on the site; web applications added to the home screen are not part of Safari and have their own counter of days of use
limit: A 2020 engineering post describing Safari's behavior then; later versions may differ. It makes a locally stored return signal unreliable for a game players open less than weekly in Safari
